Subject: Encryption evidence request: rotation, retention and sampled HSM audit logs

Hi Karthik,

As part of Greenwell Capital's SIG / CAIQ review (and our SOC2 refresh), our security team needs a few encryption & key management artifacts to close the control set for vendor risk. Can you confirm whether you can provide the following by EOD Friday (2028-06-24)? If you need more time, a short ETA would help.

Requested items (high priority):
- Key rotation registry for active KMS keys (12 months) with timestamps and operator IDs (sampling is acceptable if full export is sensitive)
- HSM operator shift logs and an example of an HSM audit entry (redacted for personal data)
- KMS access matrix (roles, permissions, who can perform key export/wrap/unwrap)
- Evidence of secure key destruction / destroy events (if any) and retention policy for retired keys
- Clarification on BYOK customers: are wrapped customer keys ever accessible in plaintext by Redwood?

Preferred delivery: secure Drive link or SFTP. If attachments are headers/stubs that's fine initially — we can iterate. We will treat any personally identifying operator metadata as sensitive and can accept redacted samples.

Appreciate your help,

Olivia Parker
Senior Security Analyst
Greenwell Capital

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide redacted samples and the rotation registry export. High-level answers up front:

- BYOK: customer-wrapped keys are never unwrapped into plaintext in Redwood's control plane; we only store wrapped material when customers opt into BYOK. We will include a short BYOK summary CSV.
- Retention/destruction: our retired-key retention policy (policy excerpt) and destroy events will be provided; for production keys we keep rotation metadata for 36 months and then archive per retention rules.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will prepare a redacted HSM shift log sample + rotation export. Irene will attach the KMS access matrix and the retention policy excerpt. I'll upload initial stubs to a secure Drive folder and share.

Deliverables we will upload by Thu EOD (2028-06-22) for your review: rotation_schedule.csv (sample export, includes key_id, rotation_time, key_version, change_type), hsm_operator_matrix.csv (roles -> operator_ids redacted), hsm_shiftlog_sample.txt (example entries), kms-rotation-report-2027Q4.pdf (summary), redacted-byok-summary.csv.

If you need notarized HSM attestation (signed statement from HSM vendor or root-of-trust attestation), let us know and we can coordinate via Security Ops — that may take additional time.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer

Hi all — attaching the initial redacted samples to the secure folder. Summary of what I uploaded:

- hsm_shiftlog_sample.txt (stub) — contains 25 sample shift entries from Sep-Dec 2027 (timestamps, operation id, event type). Usernames replaced with operator-id hashes and all IPs removed.
- rotation_schedule.csv (stub) — sample export for 12 months; includes key_id, previous_version, new_version, rotation_time, rotation_initiator (redacted).
- kms-rotation-report-2027Q4.pdf (stub) — quarter-end report showing automated rotations and metadata on manual rotations.
- redacted-byok-summary.csv (stub) — indicates BYOK customers and shows that wrapped material is maintained; column shows whether key unwrap is permitted (all NO for Redwood).
- hsm_operator_matrix.csv (stub) — role mappings; operator contact columns redacted, role permissions enumerated.

Notes and caveats:
- We can provide a signature/attestation from our HSM vendor (YubicoCloud HSM) but that requires a formal request and a small fee; we can start that process if Greenwell wants the artifact notarized.
- Some operators are named in internal runbooks; we will not provide PII.
- For destroy events: we have a small number of scheduled key retirements in 2026–2027; we will include the destroy-event audit entries but with key material hashes only (no PEMs).

Karthik / Marissa — received, thank you. The samples look good and the redactions are acceptable. A couple of follow-ups before we close the control:

1) Can you confirm whether the HSM (vendor attestation) includes a hardware-backed root-of-trust statement that covers firmware revision and tamper evidence? If not, please provide the vendor contact and we will coordinate a direct attestation request.

2) For BYOK: can you provide a one-paragraph statement we can insert into our SIG questionnaire about whether Redwood can access unwrapped customer keys (we just need the plain language assurance)?

3) For the destroy events: we will need the audit entries with event_id and hash of the key material — the stub in the folder is fine but we'd like the canonical event id mapping. Redacted operator ids are OK.

If those three items can be uploaded early next week, we'll mark the vendor evidence as complete. If the HSM attestation requires vendor coordination (and likely additional time), please let us know and we'll flag it as an open dependency in our assessment.

Best,
Olivia
